definition: The fraction of items a system answers rather than declines, and in this archive the number without which a reliability claim is unreadable. Across 3 sources its role is to price an abstention mechanism: one system's 28.5-point reduction in a hallucination proxy costs 9.6 points of it, and its reflection-depth sweep is monotone in opposite directions -- deeper reflection cutting the proxy from 0.11 to 0.06 while coverage falls 93.8 to 88.4 and effective accuracy 85.0 to 77.9, which the authors read as overcorrection and use to justify keeping reflection shallow. The same source reports its baseline comparisons in both directions, including one where it trades 2.4 points of coverage for a 13.9-point reduction in the proxy. Note that the word carries a second sense elsewhere in the archive -- the fraction of problems solvable at a large sampling budget -- which is the reasoning-boundary usage and not this one.

evidence.note: Separates hallucination into a reasoning failure and a knowledge failure, treats the first with a structured reflect-before-answering format and the second with a reward for abstaining when no sampled chain succeeds, and shows the two mechanisms are not interchangeable -- reflection alone never abstains, abstention alone never lowers the hallucination proxy.
evidence.title: REIN: Bridging the Gap between Reasoning and Reliability via Reflection and Abstention Alignment

evidence.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
evidence.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

evidence.note: Measures RLVR-trained models against their base models with pass@k at large k and finds the base wins, concluding RLVR sharpens sampling toward paths the base already had rather than adding new ones.
evidence.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

name: coverage
